newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FEDSURE SEES STRONG H2 EARNINGS GROWTH.
newsitem.headline: FEDSURE SEES STRONG H2 EARNINGS GROWTH.

text.p: South African financial services group Fedsure Holdings Ltd expects to maintain its strong earnings growth over the balance of calendar 1997, chief executive Arnold Basserabie said on Thursday.
"I've got no reason to believe that we won't at least be able to maintain, -- barring any unforeseen circumstances -- our rate of growth," Basserabie told Reuters in an interview.
The company earlier posted a 30 percent surge in earnings per share to 73.2 cents for the six months to June 30 from 56.3 cents for the previous corresponding half.
It also raised its interim dividend to 45.5 cents from 35.5 cents previously.

Fedsure's group total premium income rose 32 percent to 2.0 billion rand during the first half with Fedsure Life, the group's main insurance arm, swelling its net premium income 27 percent to 1.4 billion rand.
Fedsure's financial services activities increased their contribution to attributable income to 14 million rand, an increase of 63 percent over 1996.
"This source of income now represents 18 percent of group profits and Basserabie expects this contribution to increase further," the company said in a statement accompanying the interim figures.
Investment income from Fedsure Life rose 14 percent to 516 million rand with capital appreciation totalling 2.9 billion rand from 425 billion rand.
"That has contributed substantially to our reserves and our surplus," Basserabie said.
Fedsure Asset Management managing director Richard Derman said he was optimistic about the medium term outlook for the South African share market.
Basserabie said the group wasn't considering any offshore purchases to complement the several deals it clinched during the first half.
"We haven't shut doors this year but we're not considering anything specific at the moment," he said.
Fedsure's most recent offshore acquisition was a 200 million rand purchase of two UK-based endowment policy traders in June.
That followed Fedsure's 25 percent buy into Irish Life International (ILI) for an undisclosed sum.
Basserabie said the group would not limit itself to U.K. and Irish acquisition targets.
"We are not constraining ourselves to one jurisdiction," he said.
Fedsure's recent buys would boost the group's future earnings, Basserabie said.
"Together with other offshore acquisitions, we are looking for our offshore investments to produce 25 percent of our earnings in the medium to long term," he said.
The group was looking at refinancing the debt funding it used to make the acquisitions into permanent equity but had not finalised a structure for the equity
Basserabie said it was unlikely to involve a UK listing.
"I don't think that at this stage we will seek a listing in the UK but we certainly don't rule it out in the future."
The chief executive said the group would be unveiling a new offshore equity linked product in conjunction with ILI in about 10 days.
"It will be linked to unit trusts invested offshore but using ILI's particular investment methodology... which has for them been particularly successful."
